messages:
mike_support: FYI escalation from Acme — their backend calls to our hosted API return 401 while curl from laptop works. customer says logs show Authorization header present, but our access logs show no Authorization. Can someone look?

customer_acme: Repro steps: 1) internal service does POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat with header "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" 2) Response 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"} 3) Running same curl from devbox works fine.

jordan_eng: Can you paste the raw request headers from their failing requests (we only have what the front proxy forwards).

mike_support: Pasted from their forwarded request (redacted):
```
Host: api.redwood.example
User-Agent: acme-sync/1.2.3
Accept: application/json
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: session=abcd; apikey=sk_live_XXXX
X-Forwarded-For: 10.1.2.3
```
Note: no Authorization header in our logs. They insist they set it.

customer_acme: We do set Authorization in our code. Proxy team added an auth middleware earlier for SSO.

sarah_infra: This looks like the proxy/middleware is extracting Authorization and shoveling it into a Cookie (maybe for their SSO), removing the header before passing upstream. Some proxy plugins do that when trying to centralize tokens.

jordan_eng: That would explain why curl (bypassing corporate proxy) succeeds. Our hosted API expects Authorization header (or api_key param). We don't accept apikey cookie.

mike_support: Any quick repro we can ask them to run to confirm it's the proxy?

sarah_infra: Ask them to curl our endpoint with -x to force through their proxy and also include -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX". Then show us raw upstream headers we receive. If Authorization disappears when proxied, proxy is the culprit. Also ask them to try adding a custom header like X-Bypass-Auth: test — if that arrives we can wire a temporary rule to accept proxy-translated tokens.

customer_acme: Ran test: when going through proxy, our request shows Cookie: apikey=..., Authorization missing. When we add header X-Bypass-Auth: 1 it reaches you and we get 401 (still invalid key) — because cookie value isn't accepted as key.

jordan_eng: For a temporary workaround we can accept the cookie but only after explicit opt-in and with strict validation. However that requires infra approval. Better: ask proxy team to stop stripping/popping Authorization and forward it as-is. For nginx they'd need `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` (or ensure `proxy_pass_request_headers on;`).

sarah_infra: I'll send a short note to proxy admin template and cc customer. Template: "We are seeing Authorization header removed. Please ensure your SSO middleware forwards the original Authorization header (do not move tokens into cookies). For nginx add: `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` and avoid rewriting to Cookie for API routes"

mike_support: Sent. Customer says proxy team will test change in 30m.

customer_acme: Proxy change applied in staging, confirmed Authorization now arrives at Redwood and request returns 200. Thanks! :tada:

mike_support: Closing loop — root cause: corporate proxy middleware was extracting Authorization and translating it to a cookie, which our API doesn't accept. Mitigation: proxy config change or have client set token in query param (not recommended). Long-term: we logged internal feature request to add a secure opt-in mapping for apikey cookie but won't enable by default.

jordan_eng: Noting ticket: SR-1423 — consider a signed-cookie opt-in flow for later.

mike_support: Marking resolved.
